claim: A PANTS Crohn disease anti-TNF blood transcriptome study reported baseline immune gene-module differences associated with primary anti-TNF response and noted interferon-related genes upregulated uniquely in responders, while also reporting that baseline expression differences did not predict response with sufficient sensitivity for clinical use.
future_grounding_route: Use as Crohn treatment-response context only unless source data are imported and IFN/APC modules are scored under project definitions against the project's response-transfer framework.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: Crohn downstream IFN/APC convergence exceeds genetic proximity

project_use: Sharper Crohn treatment-response context for V50 reassessment of downstream IFN/APC convergence and transfer limits.
relationship_note: This source overlaps Crohn treatment response and interferon-related blood modules, so it is closer than generic MS-IBD genetic context; it also cautions that baseline transcriptomics was not clinically predictive enough.

source.citation: Biasci et al. Baseline Expression of Immune Gene Modules in Blood is Associated With Primary Response to Anti-TNF Therapy in Crohn's Disease Patients. Journal of Crohn's and Colitis. 2024.
source.label: PANTS Crohn anti-TNF blood immune-module response study

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: PubMed bibliographic metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: V50 stores bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrased claim only; do not redistribute article text or treat it as project-grounded evidence.

why_unverifiable: The project has not imported and rerun the PANTS expression-response data under project module definitions.
